title: Other Men's Horses

where.detail: the muster yard below the Spire

time: the spring Darrow was fourteen, at the lances' muster in Calden
last_beat: Aldric showed him the lance signal for ride wide, the open hand carried out and away, and when Darrow did it slower, stepped one pace aside to give him the room.

people.did: Held a knight's horse at Calden's muster at fourteen, caught his father's bolting grey on foot at the noon peal, stood still under a knight's crop, and learned the ride-wide signal from Aldric Vane.

facts.fact: At fourteen he came down from the Edgemoor hills behind his father's string to the lances' muster in Calden, wanting the knights to look at him, and was given a knight's horse to hold.
facts.evidence: He was fourteen, and he had come down out of the Edgemoor hills behind his father's string to be looked at.

facts.fact: When the noon peal set one of his father's greys bolting down the muster yard, he ran alongside it at the shoulder and turned its head until it stopped short of the hall steps.
facts.evidence: A horse goes where its head goes.

facts.fact: When the grey's new owner lifted a crop to him, he stood where he was rather than run from a lance's knight.
facts.evidence: He had time to think that it was a stupid reason.

facts.fact: Not one of the knights looked at him; Aldric Vane did, and showed him the lance signal for ride wide.
facts.evidence: Ride wide. Give the flank room.

people.did: Held a tower-grey beside Darrow at Calden's muster, talked a knight of his father's lance out of striking him, and showed him the ride-wide signal.

facts.fact: As a boy at Calden's muster he talked a knight with a tower on his coat out of striking Darrow, by telling him that from the steps all anyone saw was a grey that stops very well.
facts.evidence: From up there, ser, I think all anyone saw was a grey that stops very well.

facts.fact: He said the way to turn a man's temper is to say what he would want to have done and leave out what he did.
facts.evidence: You say what he'd want to have done

facts.fact: He learned the ride-wide signal from his father's lance before he could sit a horse; his father told him no captain born likes to give it, and that he would know why the first time he gave it.
facts.evidence: He says I'll know the first time I give it.

codex.name: The muster at Calden
codex.text: In spring the lances muster in a yard below the Spire: the knights go up the hall steps while boys hold their horses on the white cobbles, and the noon peal rolls down from the Spire through the yard. Greys bought that morning stand among the lances' own with the brands still raw on their near quarters (Tale 3, Piece 1).
